deviations.what: The base window uses year = fy + 0:base_years, so a class filed in year fy enters the base of focal years fy..fy+5 instead of fy+1..fy+5, which puts patents filed in year t into B(i, t) (the comment on line 15 says fy+1, but the code starts at fy+0).

notes: Everything else matches the spec: dating by filing_year, first-listed-only filter, missing/blank classes dropped, a forward window of t+1..t+3 via seq_len, the anti-join for new classes, 0 when there are no forward patents, NA when the base is empty, joins kept per firm, and deduplicated firm_year output with the five required columns. Because of the line-16 off-by-one, n_base_classes and new_classes are wrong whenever the firm filed in year t, and the base can be wrongly non-empty, giving 0 or a count where the spec requires NA.
